sources.title: Università per Stranieri di Perugia, CELI 4 (C1): competenze richieste

units.title: Mood and aspect in perspective
units.description: Choose forms that show stance, sequence and conjecture.

lessons.title: Facts, opinion and the subjunctive
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish a reported fact from a speaker’s evaluation.
lessons.takeaway: Evaluation commonly calls for the subjunctive; assertion normally uses the indicative.

objectives.label: Switch mood when a clause is evaluated rather than asserted.
objectives.explanation: A factive statement can take the indicative; a judgment introduced by è strano che takes the subjunctive.

teach.title: Assert a fact
teach.body: Dire che presents the content as reported information, with indicative.

examples.en: I say that Marta is ready.

teach.tip: Do not assume every che-clause needs the subjunctive.

teach.title: Evaluate a fact
teach.body: È strano che evaluates the situation and takes the subjunctive.

examples.it: È strano che Marta sia già pronta.
examples.en: It is strange that Marta is already ready.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: È sorprendente che Luca ___ già qui.
questions.translation: It is surprising that Luca is already here.
questions.explanation: Surprise evaluates the situation, so sia is the present subjunctive.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: È sorprendente che Luca sia già qui.

questions.prompt: Turn the fact into a sentence beginning È sorprendente che.
questions.context: Luca è già qui. Esprimi sorpresa.
questions.translation: Luca is already here; express surprise.
questions.answer: È sorprendente che Luca sia già qui.
questions.explanation: È sorprendente che calls for sia.
questions.hint: Keep the original meaning.
questions.speak: È sorprendente che Luca sia già qui.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: Il testimone dice che Luca ___ già qui.
questions.translation: The witness says that Luca is already here, as a reported fact.
questions.explanation: Dice che reports the content as fact; è is indicative.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Il testimone dice che Luca è già qui.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this meaning.
questions.context: La direttrice ritiene che la proposta sia utile.
questions.translation: The director considers the proposal useful.
questions.answer: La direttrice ritiene che la proposta sia utile.
questions.explanation: Ritiene che expresses an opinion; sia marks that stance.
questions.hint: Follow the clause relationship.
questions.speak: La direttrice ritiene che la proposta sia utile.

lessons.title: Time within past evaluations
lessons.outcome: I can place a subordinate event before or alongside a past viewpoint.
lessons.takeaway: Past viewpoint + simultaneous state: fosse; prior completed event: fosse partita.

objectives.label: Choose imperfetto or trapassato congiuntivo from relative time.
objectives.explanation: With a past main clause, contemporaneous events often use the imperfect subjunctive; earlier events use the pluperfect subjunctive.

teach.title: At the same time
teach.body: A past opinion about a simultaneous state uses the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.en: I thought she was tired.

teach.tip: Time is relative to the main clause.

teach.title: Before the viewpoint
teach.body: A completed earlier action uses the pluperfect subjunctive.

examples.en: I thought she had left.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: Alle otto pensavo che Anna ___ ancora in ufficio.
questions.translation: At eight I thought Anna was still at the office then.
questions.explanation: A state simultaneous with pensavo takes fosse.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Alle otto pensavo che Anna fosse ancora in ufficio.

questions.prompt: Rewrite using the pluperfect subjunctive.
questions.context: Pensavo che Anna partisse. La partenza era già avvenuta.
questions.translation: I thought Anna had already left.
accepted: Pensavo che Anna fosse già partita.
questions.explanation: The departure precedes pensavo, so use fosse partita.
questions.hint: Keep the original meaning.
questions.speak: Pensavo che Anna fosse partita.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: Mi sorprese che loro ___ prima del mio arrivo.
questions.translation: It surprised me that they had left before I arrived.
questions.explanation: The departure happened before the past reaction, so fossero partiti.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Mi sorprese che loro fossero partiti prima del mio arrivo.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this meaning.
questions.context: Credevo che tu avessi già letto la lettera.
questions.translation: I believed you had already read the letter.
questions.answer: Credevo che tu avessi già letto la lettera.
questions.explanation: Avessi letto locates reading before credevo.
questions.hint: Follow the clause relationship.
questions.speak: Credevo che tu avessi già letto la lettera.

lessons.title: Future forms as conjecture
lessons.outcome: I can use future forms to express a present or past guess.
lessons.takeaway: Sarà can mean “probably is”; avrà fatto can mean “probably did.”

objectives.label: Distinguish chronological future from epistemic future.
objectives.explanation: Future forms can convey a guess: sarà for a present state and sarà stato for an earlier event.

teach.title: Present guess
teach.body: A present situation may be inferred with the future.

examples.it: Sarà a casa, perché la luce è accesa.
examples.en: He is probably at home, because the light is on.

teach.tip: The context, not the form alone, determines the reading.

teach.title: Past guess
teach.body: The future perfect can conjecture about a completed event.

examples.en: He has probably forgotten the appointment.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: La luce è accesa: Giulia ___ ancora in studio.
questions.translation: The light is on: Giulia is probably still in the office.
questions.explanation: Sarà expresses a present conjecture here.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: La luce è accesa: Giulia sarà ancora in studio.

questions.prompt: Replace forse ha perso with an epistemic future perfect.
questions.context: Marco non risponde: forse ha perso il treno.
questions.translation: Marco is not answering: perhaps he missed the train.
questions.answer: Marco non risponde: avrà perso il treno.
accepted: Marco non risponde. Avrà perso il treno.
questions.explanation: Avrà perso presents a guess about an earlier event.
questions.hint: Keep the original meaning.
questions.speak: Marco non risponde: avrà perso il treno.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: Non c’è il pacco: lo ___ al vicino.
questions.translation: The parcel is missing: they have probably delivered it to the neighbor.
questions.explanation: Avranno lasciato conjectures about a completed delivery.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Non c’è il pacco: lo avranno lasciato al vicino.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this meaning.
questions.context: Sarà rimasto in ufficio fino a tardi.
questions.translation: He probably stayed at the office until late.
questions.answer: Sarà rimasto in ufficio fino a tardi.
questions.explanation: Sarà rimasto is a conjecture about a past stay.
questions.hint: Follow the clause relationship.
questions.speak: Sarà rimasto in ufficio fino a tardi.

units.title: Relations between clauses
units.description: Mark concession, purpose and precise reference.

lessons.title: Concession with sebbene and pur
lessons.outcome: I can concede a fact without losing the main claim.
lessons.takeaway: Sebbene + subjunctive; pur + gerund only when its implied subject is clear.

objectives.label: Use an explicit or implicit concessive form with the right subject.
objectives.explanation: Sebbene takes the subjunctive; pur + gerund normally shares its subject with the main clause.

teach.title: Explicit concession
teach.body: Sebbene introduces a concessive clause with the subjunctive.

examples.en: Although it is late, we will continue.

teach.title: Shared-subject reduction
teach.body: Pur + gerund keeps the main subject in view.

examples.en: Although she is tired, Marta works.

teach.tip: Avoid a dangling gerund when subjects differ.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: ___ sia costoso, il corso è molto richiesto.
questions.translation: Although it is expensive, the course is popular.
questions.explanation: Sebbene marks concession, not cause or purpose.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Sebbene sia costoso, il corso è molto richiesto.

questions.prompt: Rewrite with pur + gerund.
questions.context: Anche se è stanca, Marta lavora.
questions.translation: Although she is tired, Marta works.
questions.explanation: Marta is the subject of both clauses, so pur essendo is clear.
questions.hint: Keep the original meaning.
questions.speak: Pur essendo stanca, Marta lavora.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: Pur ___ poco tempo, abbiamo terminato.
questions.translation: Although we had little time, we finished.
questions.explanation: Pur avendo forms a shared-subject concessive clause.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Pur avendo poco tempo, abbiamo terminato.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this meaning.
questions.context: Sebbene il tempo fosse brutto, siamo usciti.
questions.translation: Although the weather was bad, we went out.
questions.answer: Sebbene il tempo fosse brutto, siamo usciti.
questions.explanation: Fosse follows concessive sebbene in a past setting.
questions.hint: Follow the clause relationship.
questions.speak: Sebbene il tempo fosse brutto, siamo usciti.

lessons.title: Cause and purpose
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish a reason from an intended result.
lessons.takeaway: Cause explains why; purpose states what someone aims to achieve.

objectives.label: Choose perché, poiché or affinché with the intended relationship.
objectives.explanation: Poiché gives a reason; affinché introduces an intended result and takes the subjunctive.

teach.title: Reason
teach.body: Poiché connects an established cause to an outcome.

examples.en: Since it is raining, we are staying inside.

teach.title: Purpose
teach.body: Affinché introduces a desired result rather than a fact.

examples.en: I speak slowly so that everyone can understand.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: Ho ripetuto la frase ___ tutti capissero.
questions.translation: I repeated the sentence so that everyone would understand.
questions.explanation: Affinché introduces a purpose and licenses capissero.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Ho ripetuto la frase affinché tutti capissero.

questions.prompt: Combine using Poiché.
questions.context: Piove; per questo restiamo dentro.
questions.translation: It is raining; for that reason we are staying indoors.
questions.explanation: Poiché presents the rain as the cause.
questions.hint: Keep the original meaning.
questions.speak: Poiché piove, restiamo dentro.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: ___ il treno era in ritardo, abbiamo avvisato Anna.
questions.translation: Since the train was late, we informed Anna.
questions.explanation: Poiché introduces the stated reason.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Poiché il treno era in ritardo, abbiamo avvisato Anna.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this meaning.
questions.context: Ti scrivo affinché tu abbia tutti i dettagli.
questions.translation: I am writing so that you have all the details.
questions.answer: Ti scrivo affinché tu abbia tutti i dettagli.
questions.explanation: Abbia follows affinché, which expresses purpose.
questions.hint: Follow the clause relationship.
questions.speak: Ti scrivo affinché tu abbia tutti i dettagli.

lessons.title: Precise relative links
lessons.outcome: I can link a relative clause to the intended noun.
lessons.takeaway: Choose the preposition required by the relation, then attach it to cui or quale.

objectives.label: Use preposition + cui or il quale to make the relationship explicit.
objectives.explanation: The governing preposition belongs before cui; a matching article precedes quale.

teach.title: Cui with a preposition
teach.body: Cui is unchanged, while the preposition shows the relation.

examples.it: La persona con cui lavoro è qui.
examples.en: The person I work with is here.

teach.title: Il quale for clarity
teach.body: Il quale agrees with its antecedent and may clarify reference.

examples.it: Il libro del quale parlo è raro.
examples.en: The book I am speaking about is rare.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: La collega ___ lavoro partirà domani.
questions.translation: The colleague with whom I work will leave tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Lavorare con qualcuno requires con cui.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: La collega con cui lavoro partirà domani.

questions.prompt: Combine with di cui.
questions.context: Parlo di questo libro. Il libro è raro.
questions.translation: I am talking about this book. The book is rare.
questions.answer: Il libro di cui parlo è raro.
questions.explanation: Parlare di takes di cui in the relative.
questions.hint: Keep the original meaning.
questions.speak: Il libro di cui parlo è raro.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: Questo è il progetto ___ abbiamo discusso ieri.
questions.translation: This is the project we discussed yesterday; discutere di un progetto.
questions.explanation: The stated verb construction is discutere di, so di cui.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Questo è il progetto di cui abbiamo discusso ieri.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this meaning.
questions.context: La città nella quale vivo è piccola.
questions.translation: The city in which I live is small.
questions.answer: La città nella quale vivo è piccola.
questions.explanation: Nella quale matches feminine città and the location relation.
questions.hint: Follow the clause relationship.
questions.speak: La città nella quale vivo è piccola.

units.title: Infinitive, participle and gerund
units.description: Compress clauses while preserving time and subject.

lessons.title: Infinitive subjects and sequence
lessons.outcome: I can reduce a clause when its subject is understood.
lessons.takeaway: Check who performs the subordinate action before reducing to an infinitive.

objectives.label: Use di + infinitive after a same-subject verb; use a full che-clause when subjects differ.
objectives.explanation: The understood subject of a dependent infinitive is constrained by its governing construction.

teach.title: Same subject
teach.body: Decidere di + infinitive normally has one subject.

examples.en: Giulia decided to leave.

teach.title: Different subjects
teach.body: A finite clause names the other subject.

examples.en: Giulia wants Marco to leave.

teach.tip: Do not silently assign Marco to Giulia’s infinitive.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: Giulia ha deciso ___ domani.
questions.translation: Giulia decided that she herself would leave tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Decidere di partire keeps Giulia as the leaver.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Giulia ha deciso di partire domani.

questions.prompt: Remove the repeated subject using an infinitive.
questions.context: Giulia desidera che Giulia possa riposare.
questions.translation: Giulia wants to rest herself.
questions.explanation: One subject permits the infinitive riposare.
questions.hint: Keep the original meaning.
questions.speak: Giulia desidera riposare.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: Giulia vuole ___ domani.
questions.translation: Giulia wants Marco, a different person, to leave tomorrow.
questions.explanation: The explicit different subject requires a finite clause.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Giulia vuole che Marco parta domani.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this meaning.
questions.context: Spero di poter tornare presto.
questions.translation: I hope I can return soon.
questions.explanation: The infinitive chain keeps the same understood subject.
questions.hint: Follow the clause relationship.
questions.speak: Spero di poter tornare presto.

lessons.title: Earlier action in reduced clauses
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish simultaneous from prior action in a reduced clause.
lessons.takeaway: Camminando overlaps; avendo finito is earlier than the main event.

objectives.label: Use simple gerund for overlap, compound gerund or past participle for prior completion.
objectives.explanation: Gerund and participial clauses need a clear understood subject and a clear time relation.

teach.title: Overlap
teach.body: The simple gerund presents overlap with the main event.

examples.en: While walking, I listened to the radio.

teach.title: Earlier completion
teach.body: The compound gerund locates an action before the main event.

examples.en: Having finished, he went out.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: ___ il rapporto, Laura uscì.
questions.translation: Having finished the report, Laura went out.
questions.explanation: Avendo finito makes completion prior to uscì.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Avendo finito il rapporto, Laura uscì.

questions.prompt: Reduce using a compound gerund.
questions.context: Dopo che ebbe letto la lettera, Marta chiamò Luca.
questions.translation: After reading the letter, Marta called Luca.
questions.answer: Avendo letto la lettera, Marta chiamò Luca.
questions.explanation: Marta performs both actions; avendo letto marks the earlier one.
questions.hint: Keep the original meaning.
questions.speak: Avendo letto la lettera, Marta chiamò Luca.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: ___ lungo il fiume, ascoltavamo gli uccelli.
questions.translation: While walking by the river, we listened to the birds.
questions.explanation: Camminando shows simultaneous activity.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Camminando lungo il fiume, ascoltavamo gli uccelli.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this meaning.
questions.context: Terminata la riunione, i colleghi uscirono.
questions.translation: Once the meeting ended, the colleagues left.
questions.answer: Terminata la riunione, i colleghi uscirono.
questions.explanation: Terminata agrees with riunione and marks a prior event.
questions.hint: Follow the clause relationship.
questions.speak: Terminata la riunione, i colleghi uscirono.

units.title: Topic and focus
units.description: Direct the reader’s attention without changing the facts.

lessons.title: Known topic and pronoun resumption
lessons.outcome: I can put a known object first and resume it clearly.
lessons.takeaway: Fronted object + matching clitic makes the topic explicit.

objectives.label: Recognize and form left dislocation with a matching clitic.
objectives.explanation: In a topicalized object, a clitic resumes the fronted noun in standard contemporary usage.

teach.title: Start with the topic
teach.body: A familiar object may come first as topic.

examples.en: The contract, I read it yesterday.

teach.title: Match the clitic
teach.body: The clitic reflects gender and number of the object.

examples.en: The letters, I mailed them.

teach.tip: The participle may agree with a preceding direct-object clitic.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: La proposta, ___abbiamo discussa ieri.
questions.translation: The proposal, we discussed it yesterday.
questions.explanation: La proposta is feminine singular, resumed by l’ before abbiamo.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: La proposta, l’abbiamo discussa ieri.

questions.prompt: Topicalize il contratto.
questions.context: Ho letto il contratto ieri. Il contratto è già noto.
questions.translation: I read the contract yesterday; the contract is already the topic.
questions.explanation: The object moves left and l’ resumes it.
questions.hint: Keep the original meaning.
questions.speak: Il contratto, l’ho letto ieri.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: Le lettere, ___ ho già spedite.
questions.translation: The letters, I have already sent them.
questions.explanation: Le is the feminine plural direct-object clitic.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Le lettere, le ho già spedite.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this meaning.
questions.context: Quel libro, lo leggerò domani.
questions.translation: That book, I will read it tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Lo resumes the masculine singular topic quel libro.
questions.hint: Follow the clause relationship.
questions.speak: Quel libro, lo leggerò domani.

lessons.title: Cleft focus and contrast
lessons.outcome: I can highlight the one person or thing that matters.
lessons.takeaway: È X che ... singles out X against alternatives.

objectives.label: Use è ... che to focus a constituent and express contrast.
objectives.explanation: A cleft presents one element as the new, contrastive focus.

teach.title: Focus the subject
teach.body: È + focused subject + che highlights who acted.

examples.en: It was Marta who signed.

teach.title: Focus an object
teach.body: The highlighted item may be an object too.

examples.en: It is this book that I am looking for.

teach.tip: Use when a contrast is intended.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: Non Luca: ___ ha firmato il modulo.
questions.translation: Not Luca: it was Marta who signed the form.
questions.explanation: È Marta che creates a cleft with Marta as focus.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: È Marta che ha firmato il modulo.

questions.prompt: Rewrite as a cleft beginning È Marta che.
questions.context: Marta ha firmato il modulo, non Luca.
questions.translation: Marta, rather than Luca, signed the form.
questions.answer: È Marta che ha firmato il modulo.
questions.explanation: The cleft isolates Marta as the contrastive signer.
questions.hint: Keep the original meaning.
questions.speak: È Marta che ha firmato il modulo.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: Non quello rosso: ___ cerco.
questions.translation: Not the red one: it is this blue book I am looking for.
questions.explanation: The cleft needs è before the focused object and che after it.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: È questo libro blu che cerco.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this meaning.
questions.context: È domani che parte il treno, non oggi.
questions.translation: The train leaves tomorrow, not today.
questions.answer: È domani che parte il treno, non oggi.
questions.explanation: The cleft contrasts domani with oggi.
questions.hint: Follow the clause relationship.
questions.speak: È domani che parte il treno, non oggi.

units.title: Register and politeness
units.description: Make requests and reports fit their audience.

lessons.title: Conditional requests and reported claims
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish a polite request from an unverified report.
lessons.takeaway: Conditional forms can soften a request or mark reported, unverified information.

objectives.label: Read the conditional from its communicative setting.
objectives.explanation: Vorrei softens a request; a journalistic conditional can distance the writer from an unverified claim.

teach.title: Polite request
teach.body: The present conditional reduces the force of a request.

examples.it: Vorrei sapere se il posto è libero.
examples.en: I would like to know whether the seat is free.

teach.title: Unconfirmed report
teach.body: The conditional can signal that a claim is reported rather than verified.

examples.en: The minister reportedly arrived yesterday.

questions.prompt: Choose the most courteous form for the specified formal email.
questions.context: Scrivi a un ufficio: “___ sapere quando apre lo sportello.”
questions.translation: A polite email to an office: “I would like to know when the counter opens.”
questions.explanation: Vorrei is a conventional courteous request in this setting.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Vorrei sapere quando apre lo sportello.

questions.prompt: Rewrite as a polite first-person request.
questions.context: Dimmi quando apre lo sportello.
questions.translation: Tell me when the counter opens; rewrite politely for an office.
questions.answer: Vorrei sapere quando apre lo sportello.
accepted: Vorrei sapere a che ora apre lo sportello.
questions.explanation: Vorrei sapere softens the direct command.
questions.hint: Keep the original meaning.
questions.speak: Vorrei sapere quando apre lo sportello.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: Secondo fonti non confermate, il ministro ___ ieri.
questions.translation: According to unconfirmed sources, the minister reportedly arrived yesterday.
questions.explanation: Sarebbe arrivato marks the report as unverified.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Secondo fonti non confermate, il ministro sarebbe arrivato ieri.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this meaning.
questions.context: Secondo il giornale, il direttore si sarebbe dimesso.
questions.translation: According to the newspaper, the director has reportedly resigned.
questions.answer: Secondo il giornale, il direttore si sarebbe dimesso.
questions.explanation: The past conditional distances the speaker from the reported claim.
questions.hint: Follow the clause relationship.
questions.speak: Secondo il giornale, il direttore si sarebbe dimesso.

lessons.title: Impersonal and passive si
lessons.outcome: I can avoid an unnecessary agent in formal information.
lessons.takeaway: Si lavora; si cercano volontari: check whether a noun is the patient.

objectives.label: Use impersonal si for general activity and passive si with plural agreement when a plural object becomes subject.
objectives.explanation: Si lavora is impersonal; si cercano volontari is a passive construction whose verb agrees with volontari.

teach.title: General activity
teach.body: Impersonal si presents an action with no named agent.

examples.en: People work quietly here.

teach.title: Plural patient
teach.body: With passive si, a plural patient controls plural agreement.

examples.en: Volunteers are being sought.

teach.tip: Do not write si cerca volontari in standard edited prose.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: Avviso: ___ volontari per sabato.
questions.translation: Notice: volunteers are being sought for Saturday.
questions.explanation: Volontari is plural, so passive si takes cercano.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Si cercano volontari per sabato.

questions.prompt: Rewrite with passive si.
questions.context: Cerchiamo due assistenti. Elimina l’agente in un annuncio.
questions.translation: We seek two assistants; remove the agent in a notice.
questions.explanation: Passive si agrees with the plural patient due assistenti.
questions.hint: Keep the original meaning.
questions.speak: Si cercano due assistenti.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: In biblioteca ___ in silenzio.
questions.translation: In the library, people work quietly.
questions.explanation: With no plural patient, the impersonal verb stays singular.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: In biblioteca si lavora in silenzio.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this meaning.
questions.context: In questo museo si conservano documenti antichi.
questions.translation: Ancient documents are kept in this museum.
questions.answer: In questo museo si conservano documenti antichi.
questions.explanation: Documenti antichi is the plural patient, so conservano agrees.
questions.hint: Follow the clause relationship.
questions.speak: In questo museo si conservano documenti antichi.

units.title: Cohesion and reference
units.description: Keep readers oriented across connected sentences.

lessons.title: Clear anaphoric reference
lessons.outcome: I can refer back to the intended item in a two-item sequence.
lessons.takeaway: If two antecedents compete, name or label the one you mean.

objectives.label: Choose il primo or il secondo when pronouns would be ambiguous.
objectives.explanation: This lesson uses explicit ordinal reference so the antecedent is recoverable without guesswork.

teach.title: Two mentioned items
teach.body: Il primo points to the first noun in a stated pair.

examples.it: Ho letto un saggio e un romanzo: il primo era breve.
examples.en: I read an essay and a novel: the first was short.

teach.title: Avoid a vague pronoun
teach.body: Repeat or label an antecedent when it matters.

examples.it: Marta ha parlato con Anna. Anna era preoccupata.
examples.en: Marta spoke to Anna. Anna was worried.

teach.tip: Lei alone could leave the reader unsure.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: Ho visitato Torino e Milano; ___ è in Piemonte.
questions.translation: I visited Turin and Milan; the first city is in Piedmont.
questions.explanation: Torino was named first, so la prima identifies it.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Ho visitato Torino e Milano; la prima è in Piemonte.

questions.prompt: Rewrite the second sentence to identify Anna explicitly.
questions.context: Marta ha parlato con Anna. Lei era preoccupata. Intendi Anna.
questions.translation: Marta spoke with Anna. Anna was worried.
questions.answer: Marta ha parlato con Anna. Anna era preoccupata.
accepted: Marta ha parlato con Anna; Anna era preoccupata.
questions.explanation: Repeating Anna removes the possible ambiguity of lei.
questions.hint: Keep the original meaning.
questions.speak: Marta ha parlato con Anna. Anna era preoccupata.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: Ho letto un saggio e un romanzo; ___ racconta una storia.
questions.translation: I read an essay and a novel; the second item tells a story.
questions.explanation: Romanzo is second, so il secondo identifies it.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Ho letto un saggio e un romanzo; il secondo racconta una storia.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this meaning.
questions.context: Abbiamo esaminato due proposte: la seconda costa meno.
questions.translation: We examined two proposals: the second costs less.
questions.answer: Abbiamo esaminato due proposte: la seconda costa meno.
questions.explanation: La seconda gives a precise link to one of the two proposals.
questions.hint: Follow the clause relationship.
questions.speak: Abbiamo esaminato due proposte: la seconda costa meno.

lessons.title: Contrast and consequence
lessons.outcome: I can choose a connector that preserves the argument.
lessons.takeaway: Tuttavia turns; pertanto follows logically.

objectives.label: Distinguish tuttavia from pertanto in linked claims.
objectives.explanation: Tuttavia introduces a contrast; pertanto introduces a consequence.

teach.title: Contrast
teach.body: Tuttavia signals an opposing fact.

examples.it: Il piano è costoso; tuttavia, è utile.
examples.en: The plan is expensive; however, it is useful.

teach.title: Consequence
teach.body: Pertanto draws an outcome from what came before.

examples.it: Il treno è fermo; pertanto, arriveremo tardi.
examples.en: The train has stopped; therefore, we will arrive late.

teach.tip: Use the logic of the two claims, not just their punctuation.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: Il corso è difficile; ___, gli studenti lo apprezzano.
questions.translation: The course is difficult; nevertheless, students appreciate it.
questions.explanation: Appreciation contrasts with the difficulty, so tuttavia.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Il corso è difficile; tuttavia, gli studenti lo apprezzano.

questions.prompt: Join the claims with pertanto.
questions.context: Il treno è fermo. Arriveremo tardi.
questions.translation: The train is stopped. We will therefore arrive late.
questions.answer: Il treno è fermo; pertanto, arriveremo tardi.
accepted: Il treno è fermo, pertanto arriveremo tardi.
questions.explanation: The late arrival follows from the stopped train.
questions.hint: Keep the original meaning.
questions.speak: Il treno è fermo; pertanto, arriveremo tardi.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: La strada è chiusa; ___, dobbiamo cambiare percorso.
questions.translation: The road is closed; therefore, we must change route.
questions.explanation: The route change is a consequence of the closure.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: La strada è chiusa; pertanto, dobbiamo cambiare percorso.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this meaning.
questions.context: La prova era complessa; tuttavia, tutti l’hanno superata.
questions.translation: The test was complex; nevertheless, everyone passed it.
questions.answer: La prova era complessa; tuttavia, tutti l’hanno superata.
questions.explanation: Tuttavia marks the unexpected positive result.
questions.hint: Follow the clause relationship.
questions.speak: La prova era complessa; tuttavia, tutti l’hanno superata.

lessons.title: Time in reported speech
lessons.outcome: I can locate a future or earlier event from a past report.
lessons.takeaway: From ha detto: sarebbe venuto is later; aveva finito is earlier.

objectives.label: Use past conditional for later-than-past and pluperfect for earlier-than-past.
objectives.explanation: Reported speech locates events relative to the original past speaking time.

teach.title: Later from then
teach.body: Sarebbe venuto is future in the past.

examples.it: Ha detto che sarebbe venuto il giorno dopo.
examples.en: He said he would come the next day.

teach.title: Earlier from then
teach.body: Aveva finito places an action before the report.

examples.it: Ha detto che aveva già finito.
examples.en: He said he had already finished.

teach.tip: Temporal adverbs may also shift in indirect speech.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: Una settimana fa Luca ha detto che ___ il giorno dopo.
questions.translation: A week ago Luca said he would come the following day.
questions.explanation: Sarebbe venuto reports a later event from yesterday’s viewpoint.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Una settimana fa Luca ha detto che sarebbe venuto il giorno dopo.

questions.prompt: Report Luca’s words one week later in indirect speech.
questions.context: Una settimana fa Luca ha detto: «Verrò domani».
questions.translation: A week ago Luca said, “I will come tomorrow.” Report it now.
questions.answer: Luca ha detto che sarebbe venuto il giorno dopo.
accepted: Luca ha detto che sarebbe venuto l’indomani.
questions.explanation: The event was future from Luca’s past statement and is today now.
questions.hint: Keep the original meaning.
questions.speak: Luca ha detto che sarebbe venuto il giorno dopo.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: Luca ha detto che ___ prima della riunione.
questions.translation: Luca said he had finished before the meeting.
questions.explanation: Aveva finito locates completion before the reported past point.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Luca ha detto che aveva finito prima della riunione.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this meaning.
questions.context: Ieri Marta ha detto che sarebbe partita oggi.
questions.translation: Yesterday Marta said she would leave today.
questions.answer: Ieri Marta ha detto che sarebbe partita oggi.
questions.explanation: Sarebbe partita is future relative to ieri.
questions.hint: Follow the clause relationship.
questions.speak: Ieri Marta ha detto che sarebbe partita oggi.

units.title: Concise formal style
units.description: Turn actions into concise, readable formal statements.

lessons.title: Actions as nouns
lessons.outcome: I can turn a full action clause into a concise noun phrase.
lessons.takeaway: Nominalize one action while keeping its participants clear.

objectives.label: Use a clear event noun and preserve its participants.
objectives.explanation: Nominalization can foreground an event, but the agent or object should remain recoverable.

teach.title: Name the event
teach.body: Chiusura names the act of closing.

examples.it: La chiusura del museo è prevista alle sei.
examples.en: The museum’s closure is scheduled for six.

teach.title: Keep the relation
teach.body: A noun phrase can retain who acted with da parte di.

examples.it: L’approvazione del piano da parte del consiglio è attesa.
examples.en: Approval of the plan by the council is expected.

teach.tip: Do not pile up nouns if a verb would be clearer.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: La ___ del museo è prevista alle sei.
questions.translation: The closure of the museum is scheduled for six.
questions.explanation: Chiusura is the event noun that fits after la.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: La chiusura del museo è prevista alle sei.

questions.prompt: Condense as one sentence beginning L’approvazione.
questions.context: Il consiglio ha approvato il piano. L’atto è importante.
questions.translation: The council approved the plan. The act is important.
questions.answer: L’approvazione del piano da parte del consiglio è importante.
questions.explanation: The noun approvazione retains both the plan and the council.
questions.hint: Keep the original meaning.
questions.speak: L’approvazione del piano da parte del consiglio è importante.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: La ___ dei dati richiede tempo.
questions.translation: Collecting the data takes time.
questions.explanation: Raccolta is the feminine event noun after la.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: La raccolta dei dati richiede tempo.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this meaning.
questions.context: La consegna dei documenti è prevista per lunedì.
questions.translation: The delivery of the documents is scheduled for Monday.
questions.answer: La consegna dei documenti è prevista per lunedì.
questions.explanation: Consegna makes the event the sentence topic.
questions.hint: Follow the clause relationship.
questions.speak: La consegna dei documenti è prevista per lunedì.

lessons.title: Compact formal clauses
lessons.outcome: I can shorten a time or condition clause without losing the logical link.
lessons.takeaway: In seguito a marks sequence; in caso di marks a condition.

objectives.label: Use a precise preposition and noun phrase for a compact formal relation.
objectives.explanation: A compact formal phrase must preserve whether it means after, before or on condition.

teach.title: After an event
teach.body: In seguito a + noun marks a later consequence.

examples.it: In seguito alla verifica, invieremo il risultato.
examples.en: After the check, we will send the result.

teach.title: Condition
teach.body: In caso di + noun marks a condition, not a cause.

examples.en: In case of delay, let us know.

teach.tip: The compact phrase must still specify the relation.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: ___ ritardo, avvisate la segreteria.
questions.translation: In case of delay, inform the office.
questions.explanation: In caso di introduces the possible condition.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: In caso di ritardo, avvisate la segreteria.

questions.prompt: Rewrite with In seguito alla verifica.
questions.context: Dopo che avremo verificato i dati, invieremo il risultato.
questions.translation: After checking the data, we will send the result.
questions.answer: In seguito alla verifica dei dati, invieremo il risultato.
questions.explanation: In seguito alla verifica preserves the later relation compactly.
questions.hint: Keep the original meaning.
questions.speak: In seguito alla verifica dei dati, invieremo il risultato.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: ___ verifica, abbiamo corretto il totale.
questions.translation: Following the check, we corrected the total.
questions.explanation: In seguito alla marks the prior check as the sequence point.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: In seguito alla verifica, abbiamo corretto il totale.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this meaning.
questions.context: In caso di pioggia, la visita sarà rinviata.
questions.translation: In case of rain, the visit will be postponed.
questions.answer: In caso di pioggia, la visita sarà rinviata.
questions.explanation: In caso di gives the condition for postponement.
questions.hint: Follow the clause relationship.
questions.speak: In caso di pioggia, la visita sarà rinviata.

units.title: Idiomatic reformulation
units.description: Restate a point accurately with compact idiomatic patterns.

lessons.title: Obligation and inevitability
lessons.outcome: I can reformulate inevitability without changing its force.
lessons.takeaway: Non posso fare a meno di X; non resta che X.

objectives.label: Use non poter fare a meno di + infinitive or non restare che + infinitive appropriately.
objectives.explanation: These constructions express that an action feels unavoidable, but differ from a bare physical inability.

teach.title: Cannot help doing
teach.body: Non poter fare a meno di means one cannot refrain from an action.

examples.it: Non posso fare a meno di sorridere.
examples.en: I cannot help smiling.

teach.title: Only option left
teach.body: Non resta che introduces the remaining course of action.

examples.en: All that remains is to wait.

teach.tip: Use the infinitive after che in this fixed pattern.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: La battuta è divertente: non posso fare a meno ___ sorridere.
questions.translation: The joke is funny: I cannot help smiling.
questions.explanation: Fare a meno takes di before the infinitive.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: La battuta è divertente: non posso fare a meno di sorridere.

questions.prompt: Use the idiom Non ci resta che.
questions.context: L’unica cosa che possiamo fare è aspettare.
questions.translation: The only thing we can do is wait.
questions.explanation: Non ci resta che expresses the only remaining option.
questions.hint: Keep the original meaning.
questions.speak: Non ci resta che aspettare.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: Il treno è partito e non ci ___ aspettare il prossimo.
questions.translation: The train has left, and all we can do is wait for the next one.
questions.explanation: Non ci resta che is the fixed idiomatic frame.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Il treno è partito e non ci resta che aspettare il prossimo.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this meaning.
questions.context: Non posso fare a meno di notarlo.
questions.translation: I cannot help noticing it.
questions.answer: Non posso fare a meno di notarlo.
questions.explanation: Di links fare a meno to the infinitive notarlo.
questions.hint: Follow the clause relationship.
questions.speak: Non posso fare a meno di notarlo.

lessons.title: Proportional comparisons
lessons.outcome: I can link two changing quantities.
lessons.takeaway: Più X, più Y describes linked change.

objectives.label: Use più ... più ... to express parallel change.
objectives.explanation: Each più starts one comparative clause; the pattern relates their changes rather than comparing two static items.

teach.title: Parallel rise
teach.body: The two quantities increase together.

examples.en: The more I read, the more I understand.

teach.title: Parallel change
teach.body: The pattern can also pair less with more.

examples.en: The less I sleep, the more tired I am.

teach.tip: Keep each clause complete enough to identify what changes.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: ___ leggo, più capisco.
questions.translation: The more I read, the more I understand.
questions.explanation: The first comparative clause begins with più.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Più leggo, più capisco.

questions.prompt: Rewrite with più ... più ... .
questions.context: Quando studio di più, capisco di più.
questions.translation: The more I study, the more I understand.
questions.explanation: The two più clauses express proportional change.
questions.hint: Keep the original meaning.
questions.speak: Più studio, più capisco.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: ___ dormo, più sono stanco.
questions.translation: The less I sleep, the more tired I am.
questions.explanation: Meno introduces the decreasing quantity.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Meno dormo, più sono stanco.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this meaning.
questions.context: Più ascolti, meno errori fai.
questions.translation: The more you listen, the fewer mistakes you make.
questions.explanation: Più and meno link opposing changes.
questions.hint: Follow the clause relationship.
questions.speak: Più ascolti, meno errori fai.

lessons.title: Correction without contradiction
lessons.outcome: I can replace an imprecise claim with a better one.
lessons.takeaway: Non tanto X quanto Y shifts the reader to the more apt description Y.

objectives.label: Use non tanto ... quanto ... to shift emphasis from one description to another.
objectives.explanation: The pattern does not always fully deny the first element; it foregrounds the second as more accurate.

teach.title: Better description
teach.body: Non tanto X quanto Y makes Y the stronger description.

examples.it: Non è tanto difficile quanto lungo.
examples.en: It is not so much difficult as long.

teach.title: Parallel elements
teach.body: Keep the two compared phrases grammatically parallel.

examples.it: Non tanto per il costo quanto per il tempo.
examples.en: Not so much because of the cost as because of the time.

teach.tip: Use the same preposition where the structure requires it.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: Il problema non è tanto il prezzo ___ il tempo necessario.
questions.translation: The problem is not so much the price as the time needed.
questions.explanation: Non tanto pairs with quanto in this contrast.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Il problema non è tanto il prezzo quanto il tempo necessario.

questions.prompt: Rewrite using non tanto ... quanto ... .
questions.context: La difficoltà principale è la durata, più che il costo.
questions.translation: The main difficulty is the duration rather than the cost.
questions.answer: Il problema non è tanto il costo quanto la durata.
questions.explanation: The frame shifts emphasis to la durata.
questions.hint: Keep the original meaning.
questions.speak: Il problema non è tanto il costo quanto la durata.

questions.prompt: Choose the form that fits the stated meaning.
questions.context: Lo faccio non tanto per abitudine ___ per necessità.
questions.translation: I do it less from habit than from necessity.
questions.explanation: The parallel phrases per abitudine and per necessità take quanto.
questions.hint: Use the clause meaning and time cue.
questions.speak: Lo faccio non tanto per abitudine quanto per necessità.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to express this meaning.
questions.context: Non era tanto arrabbiata quanto delusa.
questions.translation: She was not so much angry as disappointed.
questions.answer: Non era tanto arrabbiata quanto delusa.
questions.explanation: Quanto introduces the more accurate description delusa.
questions.hint: Follow the clause relationship.
questions.speak: Non era tanto arrabbiata quanto delusa.
